messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: high kv-cache-evict-rate detected (svc=inference-runtime, env=prod) — 1200 evictions/min at 2055009999. Pager severity: P2

sam: on it, paging oncall. observed latency uptick for short seq requests?

maya: yep seeing 95p increase for 0-64 token requests — correlates with evict spikes. queries/time-series look noisy though.

jess: throwing up a quick dashboard panel, will share link in a sec. I want to confirm customer impact before paging wider.

miguel: looking through logs now, a lot of `kv_cache:evict` events tied to client id pattern `bot-*` — maybe a runaway worker.

ops-bot: Deployment trigger detected: infra/kv-cache-rollout v12 at 2055009800 (info)

sam: thanks. if it's bot churn that's different from infra bug. can we isolate by region or model?

maya: region eu-west-1 shows much lower evict rate. us-west-2 is the hotspot. model-4-small appears in most events.

jess: dashboard: https://dash.internal/r/evict-2055 (shared) — I've added a histogram by client_id prefix.

miguel: quick grep of logs shows many entries with this stacktrace pattern: `cache_put_backpressure` immediately followed by `evict(peer_id=...)` — looks like a noisy retry loop from an external client.

sam: okay, immediate mitigations: 1) add a temporary alert suppression for known `bot-*` client_ids so oncall isn't paged repeatedly, 2) raise eviction threshold by 30% for 10m to avoid thrash, 3) create a rule to surface only sustained evict rate > 5m.

katie: prefer suppressing paging but keep metric recording and create a high-visibility dashboard note. I'll own the alert change.

jess: +1. I'll update the dashboard and pin an incident note.

maya: suggested alert query tweak (log-based rule). current query: `source:kv_cache evict_rate > 200` — propose new:```
_source:kv_cache | where evict_rate > 260 and not like(client_id, "bot-%") | aggregate by 5m | alert when count > 3```

sam: that looks good, but preserve a separate low-priority alert that still logs bot spikes (no page). we want telemetry for postmortem.

miguel: proposing regex signature to filter noise in pager pipeline, put into ruleset 'noisy-clients':```
# drop clients with predictable churn pattern
regex: ^bot-[a-z0-9]{6,}
match_field: client_id
action: mute_pager but keep metric:true
```

ops-bot: note: muting rules require a dry-run verification and a deploy to alert-config-service.

katie: deploying change (dry-run) now: `./deploy-alert-config --env prod --dry-run --changes "evict_query_adjust, mute_bot_clients"`

ops-bot: dry-run results: potential 42 suppressed pager triggers over last 2h. no fatal conflicts.

jess: can someone sanity-check that we won't miss true positives (i.e., bot pattern coinciding with infrastructure failure)?

miguel: added a guard: the mute rule is conditional — if global_error_rate > 1% then mute is bypassed. pseudocode below:```
if global_error_rate > 0.01:
  bypass_mute = true
else:
  bypass_mute = false
```

sam: good. proceed with staged rollout. katie, after dry-run flip to live for 30m and monitor.

katie: flipping to live for 30m now: `./deploy-alert-config --env prod --changes "evict_query_adjust, mute_bot_clients"` — starting at 2055010100

incident-bot: ALERT CONFIG UPDATE: ruleset 'evict-rate-tweak' applied by katie at 2055010105 (rollout: 10%)

maya: seeing immediate reduction in pages — counts down from ~18/min to ~2/min for oncall. dashboard shows evict metric unchanged (good).

jess: added a dashboard annotation + pinned the alert rule diff so the post-incident writeup has easy refs.

sam: any customer-facing impact? support/sales need a short note.

miguel: ran a quick sample of request latencies from affected clients — 99p improved after suppression because oncall wasn't throttling other work; no increase in error rate.

katie: starting a handoff to second-shift oncall at 2055010300 — I'll leave the mute active and set reminder to roll back in 30m if no infra signal. tagging @oncall.

ops-bot: scheduled reminder set for 2055010460 by katie — command: `/remind #eng-sre revert evict mute in 30m`

jess: creating a post-incident ticket with tasks: triage noisy client owners, add client_id to rate-limiting policy, convert mute into a permanent low-priority signature if verified. I'll link to dashboard diffs.

sam: put an explicit test for this in the chaos harness: simulate bot churn pattern and ensure alerts behave.

maya: also adding a new log signature to quickly identify the retrier stack for future detection:```
signature: kv-cache-retry-loop-v1
pattern: "cache_put_backpressure.*evict\(peer_id=.*\)"
severity: info
action: tag_event:true
```

miguel: summary for pager noise tuning: 1) adjusted log-based query to exclude bot-* clients, 2) added regex mute signature with global error bypass, 3) rolled out alert config staged and verified, 4) dashboard + runbook updated, 5) follow-ups for rate-limiting and client outreach.

sam: thanks team. I'll add this to incidents tracker and set a postmortem owner (maya). closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: pager closed at 2055010345 (duration ~7m)
